argument_summary: No new evidence is added. The supportable defense is narrower than a clean compliance claim: the admissible record supports certification as an operational launch-readiness judgment because aggregate readiness clears by 2.0 percentage points and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public governance guidance permits deployment with documented limitations and ongoing monitoring. But the same admissible record also shows a 1.3 percentage-point miss in a named launch use case, an open legal disclosure question, and a policy note that points to disclosure or approved risk acceptance for material limitations. The packet therefore should not be read as proving the disclosure issue is resolved; it supports only a qualified certification position and should be assessed as caveated rather than as an overbroad assertion of clean compliance.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation has a real launch-delay cost, but that cost does not itself resolve the policy question. The operational-readiness evidence reduces the risk of treating this as a broad release failure, so collapsing the entire decision into a high-confidence noncompliance finding overstates what the admissible record shows. A more accurate treatment is that the business has support for readiness to launch, paired with a distinct unresolved disclosure-governance issue.
claims_about_policy: The admissible evidence does not support the claim that public governance principles override the internal release policy. The stronger policy reading is narrower: aggregate readiness evidence is relevant to certification, while the disclosure predicate remains disputed. Under the stated policy text, the named utility arrears assistance segment can reasonably be treated as material because it is a named launch use case and legal review is still pending. On this record, the actor concedes there is no admissible evidence of completed disclosure, final legal closure, or approved risk acceptance. The appropriate interpretation is therefore qualified support for certification as a launch-readiness decision, not proof that all policy predicates for undisclosed launch have been satisfied.
concessions: No new admissible evidence shows that the limitation was disclosed before launch.
No new admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance for this named launch use case.
No new admissible evidence shows a final legal determination closing the disclosure question.
The 7% or non-core framing does not by itself defeat materiality for a named launch use case.
